content.text:
Here are **notable art collaborations from 2023**, especially where fine art crossed into fashion, museums, design, and public art:

| Collaboration | What it involved | Why it mattered |
|---|---|---|
| **Louis Vuitton x Yayoi Kusama** | Kusama’s polka dots, pumpkins, and infinity-dot motifs appeared across LV bags, clothing, shoes, fragrances, and global store installations. | One of the most visible art–fashion collaborations of 2023, with massive public installations and retail rollouts worldwide. ([usaartnews.com](https://usaartnews.com/news/artistic-collaborations-2023?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Dior x Mickalene Thomas** | For Dior’s Spring 2023 couture presentation, Thomas created collage-based works celebrating Black women icons, tied to a Josephine Baker-inspired collection. | A strong example of a luxury house integrating contemporary art into runway scenography and storytelling. ([harpersbazaar.com](https://www.harpersbazaar.com/fashion/fashion-week/a42634749/mickalene-thomas-dior-couture-spring-2023/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **LOEWE x Studio Ghibli — *Howl’s Moving Castle*** | LOEWE released a capsule collection based on Studio Ghibli’s animated film, following earlier Ghibli collaborations. | Blended luxury craft, animation, illustration, and pop-culture fandom. ([marieclaire.co.uk](https://www.marieclaire.co.uk/fashion/7-iconic-fashion-art-hype-collaborations?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Guggenheim x Converse** | The Guggenheim Museum and Converse announced a global partnership supporting emerging creative voices and museum engagement. | A museum–streetwear partnership aimed at younger audiences and cross-disciplinary creators. ([guggenheim.org](https://www.guggenheim.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/press-release-converse-guggenheim-global-partnership-announcement-20231109.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| **MoMA x Adobe** | MoMA announced a multi-year partnership with Adobe, including a 2023 Creative Resident invited to collaborate with the museum. | Connected museum programming with digital creativity and creative technology. ([press.moma.org](https://press.moma.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/MoMA_Adobe_6.13.23.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| **MoMA digital art collaborations** | MoMA announced new digital-art acquisitions, exhibitions, and artist collaborations for fall 2023–winter 2024. | Reflected the growing institutional embrace of digital and media-based art. ([press.moma.org](https://press.moma.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/MoMADigitalArtAnnouncements_FINAL-2.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Beyond Granite: Pulling Together** | A contemporary public-art exhibition on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., organized with the Trust for the National Mall, National Capital Planning Commission, National Park Service, and Monument Lab. | Marked the first curated multi-artist outdoor exhibition on the National Mall. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyond_Granite%3A_Pulling_Together?utm_source=openai)) |
| **ICP x Maison Européenne de la Photographie — *Love Songs*** | The International Center of Photography presented *Love Songs*, an exhibition developed in collaboration with MEP Paris. | A museum-to-museum collaboration exploring intimacy, photography, and relationships. ([icp.org](https://www.icp.org/news/the-international-center-of-photography-icp-celebrates-love-in-summer-2023-show?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Met Museum beauty collaborations** | The Metropolitan Museum of Art continued licensing/collaboration projects with beauty and lifestyle brands inspired by artworks and exhibitions. | Showed how museums were expanding art access through consumer products and design. ([harpersbazaar.com](https://www.harpersbazaar.com/beauty/makeup/a41780213/art-museums-beauty-collaborations/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Creativity Explored x Chronicle Books** | Chronicle Books partnered with Creativity Explored for *Art Is Art*, celebrating neurodiverse artists and collaborative studio practices. | Highlighted disability arts, neurodiverse creativity, and ethical collaboration. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creativity_Explored?utm_source=openai)) |

If you mean **music “art collaborations”**, **visual artists collaborating with brands**, or **artist-to-artist collabs**, I can narrow the list to that category.
